correctness.rationale: Direct exhaustive enumeration finds 6211 independent simplices and exact mod-two reduced ranks (1 in degree 4, 5 in degree 5, zero elsewhere), bounding rational homology. Independent signed fixed-simplex traces checked for all 240 S5×C2 automorphisms equal (-1)^flip(sign(π)-fixed_points(π)); the Hopf trace formula gives the virtual module sign⊠ε minus permutation5⊠ε. Semisimple positivity and the dimension-one upper bound force exactly sign⊠ε in degree 4, hence permutation5⊠ε in degree 5. The group identification is established by the common-neighbor triangular graph T(5) and layer swap. Quotient rational acyclicity follows from invariants over Q after barycentric subdivision. The standalone verifier was run from its actual file and returned VERIFY_OK; no finite extrapolation or unsupported integral assertion is used.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text same-object published computation establishes the wedge S^4 ∨ five S^5 but not the full S5×C2 action. Other examined bipartite Kneser sources treat Hamiltonicity or graded Betti numbers of edge ideals, not this graded rational simplicial homology module. The Kronecker-cover/Mycielskian theorem uses the double-cover independence complex as an input. Targeted research-index and public-literature queries, including aliases and representation formulas, found no statement from which the proposed graded modules follow. This is a supported but not exhaustive publication-priority assessment.
residual_risks: An unindexed, preprint-only, or differently titled equivariant computation could already establish the same two graded modules.
The 2026 same-object result establishes the nonequivariant wedge; its authors or further unpublished work might have an unindexed equivariant refinement.

value.rationale: A natural 20-vertex symmetric incidence graph has previously computed nonequivariant sphere-wedge homotopy but undetermined symmetry. The exact full-group graded module classification distinguishes the two degrees (signed one-dimensional and signed five-point permutation), shows antipodal layer exchange acts as minus one on both, and computes the rationally acyclic full-symmetry quotient. These are motivated topological invariants of the canonical graph rather than a restatement of Betti numbers or an arbitrary slice.
